evidence: All 52 criterion descriptions (40 functional, 6 polish, 3 visual, 3 gate) were read in full. None shows the row-33 defect proper: no criterion enumerates several requirements and then waives most of them. Each binary criterion is one conjunctive bar, and the injected prompts make that explicit: scored/functional/prompt.md:13 and scored/polish/prompt.md (its Evidence discipline bullet) say 'A criterion is a conjunction: every step it lists must hold, and each ends with the conditions under which it fails.' Whole-flow bundling is a known false positive for this row per SKILL.md and the internal workbook annotation. The trailing scope sentences are scope exclusions or tolerances, not waivers of an enumerated requirement: functional/judge.toml:119 'Undo behaviour is not judged here' (no Undo step is listed), :191 and :200 'A change of quote style alone is not a failure' (the bar is characters inside the string/attribute value, which a quote swap keeps), :245 and :362 pointers to other criteria, :272 'The restored picture may be static', :371 'Undo, pressed once or twice depending on how the app groups typing' (a single end state), polish/judge.toml:23 'A control the app does not have at all is scored elsewhere' (one bar over offered controls; missing controls fail functional criteria), :59 'A separate positive saved label is not required'. The 'attempt is void: repeat it once' clauses at functional/judge.toml:290 and :299 leave no second target because prompt.md:9 fails an unperformed step. constraints/judge.toml:23 states Fails/Passes/allowed-exception in one coherent rule. The three visual Likert criteria each have a single 0-5 anchor ladder. Two small wording mismatches between a criterion's body and its own closing 'Fails if' sentence remain and are reported as instances: (a) polish/judge.toml:68 cw_narrow_width_usable: the body says 'The editor's own controls must not overlap each other or be cut off' (unqualified), while the closing clause fails only 'if controls overlap or are clipped so they cannot be read or pressed' (qualified by usability). The public ask is usability (ui.md:17 'must all stay usable'). (b) functional/judge.toml:200 cw_html_format_semantics_and_undo: the body requires 'several lines with consistent two-space nesting' but its Fails list omits nesting, while the sibling JS criterion at :191 lists 'if nesting is not in two-space steps'; the same body-only pattern, with less consequence, appears at :47 (Shift+Arrow whole-grapheme selection), :74 (Shift+Tab outdent), :92 (Run shows changed tail) and :128 (readout position). Under the prompt's conjunction rule the body governs, so these are bounded, but (a) in particular gives two readings. No configured LLM judge run exists, so whether a judge actually diverges on these is unmeasured; the raw evidence index is scripted golden evidence only and does not exercise judge interpretation.
counterexample: Bounded, unmeasured: an app whose 390px editor toolbar has one button clipped by a few pixels but still readable and pressable. Read by the body sentence of cw_narrow_width_usable plus the conjunction rule it fails; read by the closing 'Fails if' sentence it passes. Similarly an HTML formatter that nests consistently with four spaces fails cw_html_format_semantics_and_undo by its body but matches none of its listed Fails conditions.
suggested_fix: In polish/judge.toml:68 change the body sentence to 'The editor's own controls must not overlap each other or be cut off so that they cannot be read or pressed', matching the Fails clause and ui.md:17. In functional/judge.toml:200 add 'if nesting is not in two-space steps' to the Fails list, as in :191; optionally add the body-only steps at :47, :74, :92 and :128 to their Fails lists.
